best_moment.what: Taught the weak 26-year-old officer plainly, and he came back as my Deputy Secretary and thanked me in Y27. That was the one time a choice paid off in a way I actually felt.

worst_moment.what: The quiet Bintan year. I rested, nothing happened, and STAND dipped for no reason the game explained. It felt like filler.

answer.held_back_by: My guess is that STAND kept falling and I never worked out why, or the game just wanted me to stay a civil servant. Maybe the politics invite was never going to come, or that mystery nomination in Y28 was never explained. I really don't know.
answer.ending_fair_why: I played honest the whole way, finished with INTEG 100 and COMP 100, and the game kept teasing a politics invite that never arrived. The card says I got to the top, which is fine, but it felt like the game dropped its own setup. The pay numbers also never matched, so I couldn't tell what the $17.77M meant.
answer.chase_next: The politics ending, since the game teased it so hard. I'd try the opposite style, like going along with being 'more visible' and playing the favours, to see if that gets the invite.
answer.play_again_why: It's 38 years of tapping and I'm tired. The first half was fun but the later years blurred together. I might try again when I'm bored, but not right now.

tone_breaks.line: Option C's 'young family' text at age ~60
tone_breaks.note: I was in my 60s, so a young family made no sense and felt like a leftover from an earlier age.
The two figures never lined up, so I couldn't trust the money, which is the whole title of the game.

answer.title_fit_why: The game was more about staying straight and getting confirmed in grades than about chasing money. My pay barely mattered to any choice I made, so 'Minister Salary' oversells it.
